# Page continuity after a pagination stress chapter {#sec-page-continuity}

This follow-on chapter proves that a later ordinary chapter still opens on a
recto after the stress chapter changes length. It also brings every PDF profile
into the 30–50 page Phase 2 specimen range without padding the build with empty
or duplicated pages.

## Invariants that survive manuscript growth {#sec-pagination-invariants}

A useful layout test should continue to describe the desired result after the
manuscript changes. Exact page numbers are poor invariants because adding one
paragraph can change every subsequent leaf. Physical parity, empty-sheet
behavior, complete text, and content containment remain meaningful even as the
page count evolves. The validator therefore discovers where each unique opener
landed and evaluates that page rather than expecting a fixed location.

The same principle applies to headings. A production title may be short today
and become longer during editing or translation. The page system must retain
its number, hierarchy, navigation destination, and full semantic text without a
manual break inserted for one trim size. A reviewer can then judge the precise
wrapping in the narrowest profile while automated checks guard the structural
properties common to all profiles.

Paragraph flow is similarly sensitive to ordinary revision. Widow and orphan
rules operate on the current line layout, so they remain useful when a sentence
is inserted or a font receives new metrics. A hard-coded page break would only
preserve the old composition and could create a new blank or half-empty page
after the next edit. The template owns pagination policy; chapter files own the
order and meaning of content.

## Fixed pages and reflowable views {#sec-fixed-and-reflowable}

PDF, HTML, and EPUB editions share semantics but not a physical model. A PDF
defines sheets, sides, trim, and a stable sequence of page coordinates. That
makes recto starts and intentionally blank versos both meaningful and testable.
A web page is a continuous viewport, while an EPUB reading system repaginates
for the device and reader preferences. Adding synthetic blank screens to those
outputs would interrupt reading without preserving a useful print convention.

The reflowable styles can still express preferences. Headings ask to remain
with following content, paragraphs request a minimum number of lines at a page
boundary, and long words are permitted to wrap before they force horizontal
scrolling. Reading systems vary in how much paged-media CSS they honor, so the
contract distinguishes a declared preference from a guaranteed sheet-level
result. No essential meaning depends on either preference being implemented.

This distinction also protects accessibility. Semantic headings remain in the
document outline even when their visual treatment changes, and a blank print
verso contributes no false navigation stop or spoken placeholder. Complete
titles remain available to search and assistive technology even when running
furniture uses a compact composition. Layout convenience never replaces the
source structure that readers and conversion tools depend on.

## Review across profiles {#sec-profile-review}

The economy trim is the first visual checkpoint for long headings because it
has the least horizontal and vertical room. The primary trim then shows whether
the same rules produce a calmer page without becoming visually unrelated. The
Letter review profile has a different purpose: generous margins and familiar
office-paper geometry make annotations convenient, but its chapter parity and
typographic hierarchy should still agree with the print interiors.

Both typesetters are evaluated independently. Their line endings and total page
counts need not match, and trying to force them into pixel equality would hide
the strengths and limitations we need to compare later. They must agree on the
book structure, reading order, page dimensions, recto policy, blank-page
furniture, heading hierarchy, and selected font families. A difference outside
those invariants becomes evidence for the eventual backend decision rather than
an automatic defect.

Visual inspection complements those checks. It catches an overfull heading
whose text still extracts correctly, an awkward running head that remains
technically inside the page, or a sequence of loose bottoms that makes spreads
feel unstable. The stress chapters concentrate these risks into a few pages so
a reviewer does not have to search an entire manuscript. The acceptance notes
record which pages and profiles deserve attention after a theme change.

## Phase 2 handoff {#sec-phase-two-handoff}

With these specimens in place, the reference book has a coherent page system,
shared typography, output-specific reflow behavior, explicit language support,
and repeatable layout checks. Later roadmap phases can add code, math, figures,
tables, notes, and semantic components without reopening basic decisions about
which side a chapter begins on or whether an empty verso carries furniture.

Those later components will create new pagination pressures. A tall figure may
leave a heading near the foot of a page, a code listing may resist breaking,
and a translated caption may become twice as long. Each feature should add its
own minimal stress case and preserve the invariants established here. The page
system is therefore a foundation for further testing, not a claim that every
future composition problem has already been solved.

The practical handoff is intentionally modest: authors write semantic chapters
without manual page commands, the build applies profile geometry and medium-
appropriate flow rules, automated checks catch structural regressions, and a
short visual review judges composition. That division of responsibility keeps
the template simple to use while leaving enough control for demanding technical
books and future publication profiles.
